extracted.intended_audience: science journalists, press officers, research communications staff, journal editors
extracted.subtask_description: Posts and guidance about how scientific-information embargoes should be handled, when embargos may be lifted, how breaches are investigated, and what actions publishers and press officers should take. Focused on coordination between journals, conferences, PR services, and media.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lift embargo early when information is already public
rubrics_metrics.description: Publishers may lift an embargo early if the information has entered the public domain or media coverage makes it unreasonable to continue the embargo.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples from page: 'PNAS is lifting the embargo early on the following paper' and Science: 'the embargo is being lifted ... because this information has entered the public domain.' Use early lift to allow reporters to publish freely once material is already widely available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adhere to embargo timing and avoid premature promotion
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not promote or publicize embargoed material before the stated embargo time; doing so is a violation of embargo policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit quote: 'It is a violation of our embargo policy to promote a JAMA study before publication.' Example: Good Morning America promoted a JAMA study before publication and was judged to have broken the embargo even though their story contained no data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigate embargo breaks and assess intent before sanctioning
rubrics_metrics.description: When an embargo is broken, the responsible organization should investigate circumstances and consider intent (unintentional mistake vs deliberate breach) before deciding on sanctions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: European Heart Journal / Straits Times — investigation found the break unintentional and 'no further action' was taken. ASCO said it is 'investigating the reasons for this embargo break.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Publishers may request takedown or contact outlets after a break
rubrics_metrics.description: If an outlet posts embargoed material early, publishers or journal PR may contact the outlet to request removal or discuss the breach.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: AACR/Clinical Cancer Research contacted CNN to see if they could take down an early item: 'a press officer ... told him that they'd contact CNN to see if they could take down the item.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Embargoes are time-specified and often tied to conference schedules
rubrics_metrics.description: Conference abstracts and journal articles have explicit embargo lift times (e.g., 'embargo lifts at 6 p.m. Eastern'), and these times should be respected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: ASCO abstracts embargoed until a fixed time: 'the embargo on most conference abstracts lifting tonight at 6 p.m. Eastern.' Organizers should communicate exact lift times to media lists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Press officers must communicate embargo status and any early lifts clearly
rubrics_metrics.description: Media/press officers should notify their media lists promptly about embargo lifts, early lifts, and the scope of which items remain under embargo.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: PNAS message to media list specifying which items had embargo lifted and that 'All other articles are under the scheduled embargo.' ESHRE press officer Emma Mason sending messages after a lift.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability of abstracts or prior presentations can complicate embargo enforcement
rubrics_metrics.description: If abstracts or prior conference presentations are freely available, enforcing an embargo may be difficult and may lead to early lifts or no sanctions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: 'Menopause study embargo lifted early ... abstracts were freely available' — when content is accessible, maintaining an embargo can be unreasonable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distribution channels (e.g., PR Newswire) can cause inadvertent embargo breaks
rubrics_metrics.description: Using wire services or other broad distribution channels without careful timing can lead to embargoed material being posted early.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: ASCO rituximab abstract — 'a release about the study went out early this morning on PR Newswire' which contributed to an embargo break. Coordinate distribution timing and channels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusive coverage vs embargo fairness: handling exclusives carefully
rubrics_metrics.description: Granting exclusives while holding other reporters to an embargo can be controversial and may prompt scrutiny if others publish similar content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: A PR agency gave Nick Kristof an exclusive while holding others to an embargo; the page notes tension between exclusives and general embargo enforcement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publishers may lift embargos universally after widespread early coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: When multiple outlets publish early or leaks make it unreasonable to uphold an embargo, publishers may lift the embargo for everyone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Reuters published after others 'made it unreasonable to continue to uphold the embargo,' and Science lifted its embargo 'effective immediately ... so that reporters may freely publish their coverage now.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Cultural norm: treat embargoes as 'sacred' and reinforce staff reminders/training
rubrics_metrics.description: Organizations often treat embargoes as sacrosanct and remind staff or partners about their importance; breaches may prompt internal reminders or disciplining of responsible staff.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example wording: 'embargoes are sacred' and Straits Times 'the perpetrator has been taken to task ... the rest of the team has been reminded about the fact that 'embargoes are sacred'.' Use training and clear policies to prevent mistakes.
